ios.desc:
Sudecku is Sudoku with a deck of cards in your hand.

The grid is the same 9×9 you already know, but you just fill it differently. Every number you place is a card you've drawn. Alongside the numbers there are power cards that can fill a stubborn cell, check your work, or reshuffle your hand when you're stuck. Sudoku with card strategy!

What's in it:

- A new puzzle every day, at several difficulty levels
- Number and power cards you unlock over time and build into your own deck
- High scores that actually unlock things, so a good run gets you stronger cards
- A clean layout for iPhone and iPad with nothing in the way of the puzzle

I started this as a small experiment: what if Sudoku had a little risk in it? It turned out to be more fun than expected, and it's been shaped slowly, one piece at a time!

If you like Sudoku but wish it pushed back a bit more, or you like card games and want something quieter, give it a try.

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I'm excited to share Sudecku, my first iOS game. It combines classic Sudoku with deck-building strategy. If you enjoy logic puzzles or card games, you might enjoy Sudecku.

The idea started from playing a lot of Sudoku with my wife and watching Cracking the Cryptic solve some wild sudoku variants. I was also inspired by Balatro, which showed how much depth and replayability can be added to a simple cards game. That got me thinking about what would happen if Sudoku had power-ups sort of like Uno action cards or Balatro’s combos, and deck-building mechanics. After countless hours of playtesting and feedback (mostly from my wife), Sudecku finally came together.

It's a paid app. One-time purchase kind of deal. There are no in-app purchases or ads. You get the full game up front. It's also iOS only for now, but I'm definitely open to releasing on other platforms if there's demand.

You can check it out here:

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/sudecku/id6747517140

This was a labor of love for me, and I'd love to hear what you think, any feedback or questions are welcome.

Thanks for checking it out!

(Happy to answer any questions about the game or the development.)

PS. If you'd like to try the game but can't pay for it for some reason, please email me (me at my first name dot com) and I'll happily provide you with a promocode.

Thanks!
